I am seeing this with the Labwc Wayland compositor, too.
For the FIFO protocol error, few compositors have it implemented, see the table in:
[wp_fifo_manager_v1](https://wayland.app/protocols/fifo-v1#wp_fifo_manager_v1)

I'm getting the same FIFO error. Though I'm not getting the decoration manager error, it adds extra space on the top and bottom of the window and thinks the UI thinks that my mouse is lower than it actually is. Which seems like it might be related to the window decorations(the extra space disappears and the mouse returns to normal when i enter fullscreen).

![](https://i.imgur.com/LRY22zl.png)

WM: Hyprland
Godot Version: 4.5.1
Distro: Arch

I've also tried to run it with `--display-server x11` to see if it was a wayland thing but it still gave the exact same error(the error still happens in the wayland thread). Which is a little weird because the option doesn't do anything even if I enter total gibberish as the display server.

@Unfinished632 same issue here on Hyprland, for now I unchecked `Prefer Wayland` in `Editor>Editor Settings>Run>Platforms` to work with xwayland instead.
The problem seems to be fixed for me. Ig it was a non-godot issue. Edit: The problem still accurs with popup windows.

Hi, those are not errors, they are warnings and are absolutely not critical. The Wayland ecosystem is made of many extensions, called "protocols" in Wayland parlance. We try to support as many compositors as possible, with any combination of protocols.

The purpose of those warnings is to let you, the user, know why some feature might be missing. FIFO support is still not implemented in many compositors. In simple words it allows to maximize GPU throughput and have a stable frame timing. Games will still work without it (and we put a lot of care into that) but we can't guarantee ideal frame timing.

The XDG decoration manager protocol is somewhat different, as it's implemented only by compositors which expose server-side decorations. In this case, it's perfectly normal for it to be missing, and it informs you that libdecor will draw decorations, if available on your machine.

Regarding the decoration issue, it's completely unrelated to the warning and I'd appreciate a separate issue report for that.

Hope that clears up any doubt.
